hypothesis_update: Hypothesis: lower_compose promises to reject missing/invalid components, unknown aliases, and incompatible interfaces via CoreError, but a likely defect is a path where one of these conditions is not checked before state is mutated or rewritten (silent fallback/misclassification), producing a corrupt or incorrect composition instead of an error. I need the target body to confirm the sequence of checks and identify which callee (most likely parse_component for missing/invalid components, or sync_action/alias-resolution for unknown aliases) guards the promised rejection.
rationale: I have only the overview so far, and it names four callees (parse_component, rewrite_component_item, rewrite_compose_statements, sync_action) but no body. The contract to be verified — CoreError for missing/invalid components, unknown aliases, or incompatible interfaces — is a property of lower_compose's own control flow, not of any single callee. Reading lines 249-372 is the minimal, highest-leverage move: it shows the ordering of validation vs. mutation, which error branches exist, and which of the four callees actually sit on the error path, so that rounds 2-3 can target the specific callee that may swallow or misclassify an error rather than guessing among all twelve cards.
